reviews.title: Payment transfers in indefinite limbo
reviews.text: I received two emails well over a month ago indicating that they could not transfer funds that had been sent to me and that I should contact support, which I did…6 times. All I was told was that they were, “Looking into it”. At one point, they said they didn’t have any account or bank information on file for me, since I cancelled the app due to my extreme frustration with them and their support.  Funny, they had no problem continuing to charge me the monthly subscription fee, drawing the funds from my bank acct. before I complained to them about that and they eventually reversed that charge. Which means You DO have an account and a bank source for me! Bottom line: they are still holding my money, have made NO effort to resolve the issue or respond back to my inquiries, and now I’m forced to take this matter up with BBB and CFPB.

reviews.title: App was ok until GREED took over!

And to make these changes KNOWING this app is usually court ordered is quite egregious. Unless you’re ready to pay $100 a year for basic features that barely work, I DO NOT RECOMMEND. And pick another option if suggested through the court.

reviews.title: Unable to make calls
reviews.text:
AppClose is the only way I am able to communicate with my child, and for three consecutive days, I have been unable to make a single successful phone call.

Every time I attempt to call, I immediately receive a message saying “user is busy.” I can try 20 times a day, and all 20 attempts result in the same message without the phone even ringing.

Both my iPhone and the AppClose app are updated to their latest versions. I have contacted customer support and received absolutely no response.

This is extremely frustrating and unacceptable, especially for an application designed to help parents communicate with their children. When this app is the only authorized way to contact your child, a problem like this is not a minor inconvenience. It means going days without being able to speak to your own child.

Three days without communication and no response from customer support is completely unacceptable.

reviews.title: Warning re:payments… inferior product and my ex agrees

Just be aware that for the first 30 days of active use, you won’t be able to make timely payments over $100.  Also, there is no option to pay outside of the app, such as by check, which the competing software does allow.  It’s a cheaper platform but definitely inferior and my ex agrees.  Hey, at least we can agree on that!

reviews.title: An app that should not be trusted with court-related co-parenting.
reviews.text:
Repeated notification failures create constant anxiety and a serious risk that crucial messages about children will be missed. The IT support is appalling: problems are reported, complaints are closed without resolution, and nobody takes responsibility or provides a lasting fix.

This is not a minor inconvenience—it can damage communication, disrupt contact and wrongly make a parent appear unresponsive. Any app used in legal proceedings must be dependable. This one is dangerously unreliable and, in my experience, utterly unfit for purpose.

Parents should avoid it. Solicitors and courts should stop recommending it.

reviews.title: Poor Customer Support
reviews.text:
Horrible app, and even worse customer support.

I’ve been having a bug issue for over a month, related to notifications. I contacted AppClose directly for customer support. After providing them with all relevant info that they asked for, the issue has still not been resolved. I followed up with them, and all I received is a canned, generic response. No resolution or update to my issue, even though they promise to “fix any issues right away”, as explained in the App Store. I don’t understand the delay or the lack of customer support.

Here is the canned, generic response I received: “We sincerely apologize for the delay in providing a solution. We understand the inconvenience this has caused and are actively working to resolve the issue.” Translation: We don’t care about the issues you’re experiencing, and are unable to provide a resolution. We do not value you as a customer.

Looking at other customer reviews, there seems to be a common theme. Too many bugs, not enough support.

My advice, if you are a parent looking for a co-parenting app, especially if it’s going to be court-ordered, look elsewhere. Recommend a different app to be used with the court, citing that AppClose has too many bugs and does not provide adequate customer support. Buyers beware!

It seems this company bit off more than it can chew.

reviews.title: Limited Support
reviews.text:

Read the comments… They don’t care about the user, it’s a money grab. Uninstall reinstall doesn’t help. No bulk notification clear all button. Development request ignored and instead you get a response we are the #1 app ordered by courts. 

Dishonest business model if ask me. Make it free, give it to everyone, get it court ordered. Once we get enough users of the free product hit them with a price tag because guess what? A huge chunk of the user base is locked in by court order. Which explains why they don’t care about the end user. They say they work with low income families and throw out random #s of discounts gave with no data to back it.

Anyway if someone has the option to read reviews on App Close before they are court order, I would suggest exploring other options. The price for this app is basically what the other apps charge.

reviews.title: Worse Than Free Alternatives
reviews.text:
This app is absolutely terrible. The video chat feature is painfully slow and unreliable. Every time I try to start a video call, I end up waiting 10–15 seconds before the video even begins to work—if it works at all. It’s unbelievable that anyone would expect people to pay for this when free apps like FaceTime and WhatsApp perform dramatically better.

The app feels buggy, outdated, and frustrating to use. One of the most annoying issues is the notification system. No matter what I do, message notifications refuse to clear, even after I’ve read every message. The badges just sit there permanently, constantly grabbing my attention and making it look like I have unread messages when I don’t.

Paying for an app that performs worse than free alternatives is ridiculous. This app is a complete waste of money and one of the most frustrating apps I’ve ever used. If I could delete it from existence and never deal with it again, I would.

reviews.title: Hard pass
reviews.text:
Only after you sign up and provide your personal information do they tell you that you’ve just started a 60-day free trial.

The marketing creates the impression that the service is free, but it isn’t. At least some competitors are more transparent about their pricing and trial structure upfront.

The onboarding process also raised concerns. The app repeatedly informed me that it had generated an invitation for my co-parent and asked whether I wanted to send it, despite the fact that I had never provided that person’s email address.

What bothers me most is the business model. Family courts increasingly encourage or recommend these apps, creating a captive audience of parents who often have little choice but to use them. Yet many of these services put basic functionality behind subscriptions and recurring fees.

The company states that fee waivers may be available for qualifying users, but it is unclear how those programs operate or who ultimately bears the cost. Greater transparency would be welcome.

To me, this is a perfect example of capitalism at its worst: taking a difficult family situation, inserting a middleman, collecting personal information, and then charging people for services they may feel pressured to use. When an industry profits from conflict rather than solving it, consumers should be skeptical.

Hard pass.

reviews.title: Way too complex and hard to navigate
reviews.text:
There’s a bunch of features here, and I’m sure they’re all very valuable, but there is absolutely no way to Taylor the experience to anyone’s individual situations.

They also bury things you use a lot deep down scrolling lists, and there is no such thing as a easy one click operation for literally anything inside this app.

I think it serves a purpose, but the actual experience of using the app itself is one of the worst I’ve ever had, and I may be jaded because I work in building saas applications, but it’s obvious whoever they hired to do the UX and UI of this app has never actually talked to any user.  

If there was any worthwhile competitive to this, I would switch instantly.  

If you read a lot of the five star reviews here, it’s everyone complaining about the same thing, but for some reason, people don’t understand that you can give less than five stars when you’re not happy or the app doesn’t deserve it.

reviews.text: Forced by court to download this app for co parenting. Now 3 years later I have to pay for it… sad that this went from helping parents to stealing from them when they are already struggling.

reviews.title: Needs fix!!!
reviews.text: The app constantly shows 1 notification and the message never changes to read even after I open and respond. It also doesn’t notify me of calls or messages.

reviews.title: Notification that will not go away
reviews.text:
I've been using this app for almost 2 years now, and all of a sudden, within the last couple weeks, I have a notification on my AppClose icon that will not go away, no matter what I do, it’s driving me nuts! I've contacted customer service and they haven’t done anything.

I’m running iOS 26.3.1

Anyone else having this problem? It keeps showing I have an unread notification, however, I’ve read all the messages, but it still shows a notification icon.

reviews.title: Not great
reviews.text: Would freeze a lot and show that a message was there to be read but the notification would never clear. No longer using it

reviews.title: The worst app
reviews.text: I’ve never seen a less intuitive and more difficult app.

reviews.title: Payment Doesn’t Work; Calendar Doesn’t Work; Not Worth It
reviews.text: This was fine when it was free… sort of. The calendar has never worked well with schedules that don’t fit the developer’s little boxes. Now the payment doesn’t work because they say my DOB on their app and my DOB on my license don’t match (even though they do). Then they started charging, further decreasing the value of the application. There are free ways to do the same thing built into your iPhone. This isn’t worth it.

reviews.title: AppClose hides that they have financial transaction limits
reviews.text:
I am updating my review to state emphatically that AppClose Does not disclose that it has financial limits for transactions in their coparenting reimbursement tools.   They are incredibly difficult to use, and if you need to transact a significant amount of money to your coparent, you need to use a different app because this one will limit you.  Support response has been ghosting me for the last month on my inquiries and requests to increase the transaction limit.  This app is good for communication logging and that is all.

Been using AppClose for a couple of years for communication and it works well for that.  The calendar is extremely buggy and not intuitive.  Worst of all is the ipayou feature!  They don’t mention the financial transfer limits but they imposed a $500 limit for the first 90 days and no details of whether or how to increase the limit.  I have ongoing transfers to make for two children and this doesn’t even come close to the amount I have to pay for medical bills and extracurricular activities.  The financial cap makes this worthless for financial transactions.  Unless you are only going to use the app for communications, definitely look at other apps until they fix the calendar and financial pieces.

reviews.title: Hello? Hello? Is anyone there???
reviews.text: There is absolutely no customer support at all. I’ve been sending emails since December and I’ve got no response. They forced you to pay a subscription but you can’t talk to a person when a question or concern arrives? And this is the number 1 app??? Shane Shane Shane. I will not recommend this app

reviews.title: For use of co parenting
reviews.text: Rubbish and can’t cancel my subscription

reviews.title: Scam…..
reviews.text:
A completely waste of money and time at first, the app was free for thousands and thousands of parents and I agreed to using it because that’s what the other parent wanted and the judge said yeah that’s fine to use it so now I have it in my parenting plan to use this app and half of the time it doesn’t work but all the parents that we’re on here that now have this app in a court order pay for it where it was free and this app is completely unnecessary. You could get all documents tax through your cellular data plan or provider and if the other parent it
becomes hostile. What’s this app gonna do absolutely nothing you can block people on your phone with or without this app if it becomes hostile it really doesn’t make any sense to have this app when you can have all the proof at your fingertips anytime you want through your cellular plan it’s easy to export data. This app is just more of a violation of privacy than anything and half of the time it doesn’t work right I have to restart the app to send messages so many times because it says it failed delivery.

reviews.title: Service Failure – Court-Ordered Communication App
reviews.text:
This app is currently preventing court-ordered communication between my child and his father. I am a paid subscriber, yet for over two weeks the app has not functioned properly, and support responses have been slow and ineffective.

Because this platform is court-ordered, technical failures create serious legal consequences. When an app is used for mandated communication, reliability and timely support are critical. Unfortunately, that has not been my experience.

I have submitted support requests and emphasized the urgency, but the issue remains unresolved. At this point, I am paying for a service that is not being provided and am left documenting outages to protect myself legally.

I hope the company improves both its technical stability and its customer support response times, especially for users relying on this app for court compliance.

reviews.title: Messages
reviews.text: I really dislike that you can’t search messages by keywords like you can in standard text messaging. Without this feature. It’s nearly impossible to find messages from weeks ago, which makes the app pretty much useless for keeping track of past conversations.

reviews.title: No point.
reviews.text: Had been using this for quite some months after court. But now has a subscription on 8.99 a month which sadly some people can’t afford.

reviews.title: Dreadful support
reviews.text: Before this app changed to a subscription service I found very user friendly and perfect for communication. I have now subscribed to the monthly subscription service as they no longer offer a free service - despite AppClose deducting a monthly fee when I attempt to use the app I’m told that I need to subscribe. 7 emails to support later - no response or resolution. Dreadful!

reviews.title: Fraud
reviews.text: Forced into a subscription through the court, originally it was free, but now I’m forced to pay for the subscription. Evil and disgusting world.

reviews.title: Was better
reviews.text:
I have contacted support last year. I haven’t heard back yet. The conversations in the app are being cut off when you enter them. Is there a new limit as to the number of characters you can use? This is a new thing since December. Yes, the app and my phone’s operating system is up to date. The phone has been restarted. AppClose became a subscription app since January which is ok because it a court ordered thing mainly because my coparent is my coparent.  Sharing medical information between coparents is difficult when the information is not being conveyed because the app cuts off the message!

Update: I was contacted by the developer. The problem has not been solved.

reviews.title: Was free now paid
reviews.text: Not great as it was a free app, now it’s paid

reviews.title: Poor
reviews.text: Not bad for a free app. Terrible for a paid app. Especially bad as both parents have to pay.

reviews.title: Terrible customer service
reviews.text: There’s a technical issue with the app. It requires you to receive a two step verification. Out of nowhere, I was not able to log into my account because it would send me an email one time password, but I was never receiving the emails. They were not going to my spam, they were not being sent out at all. So far it’s been over a week and I haven’t been able to get any help from customer support. They just say they won’t look into it and get back to me. I had custody court, which I made them aware of, and I was not able to download any of my critical conversations. I cannot believe the lack of customer support.

reviews.title: Customer service is horrible
reviews.text: I tried for two weeks to get an issue with my subscription resolved to only be answered with “we will look into this”. I had to go through my bank to dispute the transaction. On top of that there is no telephone customer support. I left voicemails to never be answered. An absolute horrible experience. The developer responded to my review saying they cannot handle the issue in a public forum and to reach out. I have reached out over 15 times via email and left 2 messages because you have no telephone support, sir. I have filed a claim with the better business bureau and again disputed my transaction. Y’all can’t even handle issues on a public forum let alone actual issues with the app.

reviews.title: Fraudulent payments taken
reviews.text: AppClose have duplicated payments without authorisation and refused to return contact when a refund has been requested. Avoid this parenting app and use a reputable one who don’t fraudulently take payments then refuse to provide basic customer support for their own bad business practices.

reviews.title: Don’t bother
reviews.text:
It is the most downloaded app because it was free. Now it is not free, it will not be the most downloaded.
You have reeled people in asa free app and then you have now charged a ridiculous amount of money per month to access it. 60 day trial means nothing bla bla. Boring, it was free now you charge grossly. Your response changes nothing.

reviews.title: No longer free
reviews.text: I was okay with using the app it was brought up by my lawyer and a judge. It was a healthier way of communicating with the other parent. We don’t have any other way of communication but through this app and I don’t use it often it’s just occasionally when there’s an emergency or we need to switch weekends, etc… now the are charging to use it every month I don’t find that necessary because I don’t use it often now I have to look for another to reach out to the other parent because we don’t have each others number and his partner feels it’s disrespectful to have each others number. This is stressful. It was a great app before. I have zero access to all the pictures and conversations from the past until I pay. This is ridiculous!

reviews.title: Pure con
reviews.text: Sorry no, I’m not going to start paying for features that you remove from a free app, nope! Pure greed

reviews.title: Average app, nonexistent customer service
reviews.text:
I was led to believe that this app was one of the top few apps in this field. However, the main piece of functionality that I wanted that would allow three way communication and calendar management (as well as private communication me and my co parent) with my teenage child and the other parent was not part of the app. This seems fundamental to me, and especially since the UK courts have ordered me and my co parent to use an app. What has pushed me to write this review and give it one star is the simply appalling level of support I have received from appclose. The support email address is a black hole, with not even a reply to acknowledge my support request. No support ticket number, no replies despite repeated emails. I have requested after a few days of using the app and being disappointed with zero response to any emails, a refund of my subscription, again with no response. Customer service very poor, and for a topic that is sensitive for parents I would have expected much better, and it feels like that have taken my money and simply disappeared.

Further detail. I received the following email weeks later with still no actual email from their support team. They clearly think I am an idiot and I haven’t checked my spam folder! Terrible support service!!! 

‘AppClose remains court-trusted and the highest-rated, most downloaded co-parenting app for a reason. The platform supports multi-party communication and shared calendars with role-based permissions designed to meet court

reviews.title: Not free anymore
reviews.text:
UPDATE

Developers explanation doesn’t change the fact, that I am dealing with a person who is refusing to pay for any app so it doesn’t matter if AppClose is cheaper than other apps or not. I used to have this app as the safest way possible to contact an abusive ex-partner and now this was taken away from me. Just because other apps are all paid for, it doesn’t mean you have to follow. You obviously don’t care about the kids or the parents. I would happily only use the massaging option for free. No need for the other features like call recording etc. And you know this cause probably people were happy with the free version and didn’t pay for the extra features. So you just charge now cause you want more money. Simple.

This used to be a great app. Now you made it all subscription based, you are forcing me to go back to something that doesn’t serve the purpose but my ex clearly stated that he is not paying, and I cannot force him. You gave him a great excuse to come off a parenting app so he can continue his hurtful behaviour somewhere where he can delete it after.

reviews.title: Not worth it!
reviews.text:
So INCREDIBLY disappointed in this app! This app was court ordered by a judge for communication with my ex so he could stay in touch with our child since we had a DV case. First of all, the app glitches CONSTANTLY! They just recently gave you an option to record phone calls but you have to pay for it which is crazy overpriced. And now you have to pay for a subscription just to use the app in general! I am required to use this specific app to protect me from my ex and I have to pay a monthly fee for it now when it doesn’t even work that well or do enough to protect me. Absolutely outrageous! I would give ZERO stars if I could.

**Update** I saw the response from AppClose. The fee waiver option is a joke! There’s only 3 ways to qualify. If you don’t meet one of those 3 options, it doesn’t matter. I’ve talked to your customer service multiple times because this app messes up so much and everyone is extremely rude. Don’t pretend to be sympathetic to family issues when all you care about is how you can make more and more money off victims of domestic violence.

reviews.title: Extortion at its finest.
reviews.text:
I don’t need or use any of the “new” “paid” features and are forced to pay for them. It needs to go back to the previous model of paid recorded calls and free texting like it was and has been for a long while.

EDIT: Response I resolved from AppClose:

"We appreciate your feedback and the opportunity to clarify. Each month, AppClose facilitates over 27 million secure interactions including messages, calls, shared events, expenses, and custody updates preserved as unalterable, court ready records. After nearly a decade of service, we’re introducing one all inclusive plan beginning January 1, 2026, announced with 60 days’ notice. The $8.99 per month plan has no tiers, upsells, or hidden fees and includes fee waivers for families in need, plus a 60 day free trial for new users. Unlike other apps that limit features, require annual prepay, or charge extra for calls, recordings, storage, or exports, AppClose remains unlimited, ad free, and court trusted. We encourage families to compare plans and prices across co-parenting apps, along with tools, reviews, and restrictions, and choose what best supports their co parenting needs."

Still hold my position that it is a crock that this is a paid app!

reviews.title: Was good until they charged a fee
reviews.text: Was a good app to use. The co-parent refused to pay the new subscription it’s now made communication difficult.

reviews.title: Was good before greed won
reviews.text: I could understand the new features like calls and call recording being paywalled. I could even understand changing it to subscription for existing features like location check in. But locking the messaging too is absolutely greed and it was funny to watch them spam us with bait emails to get a “legacy discount” and it was so overpriced even at a discounted price. Legacy users should get unlocked messages for life, period. Paywall everything else, I don’t care. I would’ve paid for that but the audacity to lock the messages too just shows they aren’t loyal to us so why should I be loyal to them? I’d rather find a better app if I’m going to be paying.

reviews.title: NOT FREE ANYMORE
reviews.text: Other parent refuses to pay on his end - now causing so much grief!

reviews.title: Good enough, terrible customer service
reviews.text: This app was not great but good enough when free, but recently changed to a paid app. This caused disagreement with my coparent who doesn’t want to pay for this service and will likely force us back to court. In the meantime, I had questions about the paid version and the supposed “solo” version. There is no one to talk to. None of the questions I have sent in the last month have been answered. I signed up for the oaid account on the last day before my free account shut down because the website says I can still message and create events for someone who is not in the app. The coparent cannot view any of those things but receives a notification. This is not worth me paying for if it does not allow that oerson to view it. Overall, it was fine when free but a very poor product if you’re charging a monthly fee for it.

reviews.title: What a shame, I had high hopes for this company.
reviews.text: This was a great app for parents to use.  It gave steady communication with export data available. When users needed a court approved app that would monitor conversations at no cost to the parents involved, they used AppClose. Until they wanted to charge parents who are already going through a rough situation. You had the right idea once upon a time by making a tough situation a little easier to bear by providing the service free to those who used it. Yes you may be charging 8.99$/mo but, Why would you add another thing to charge already strapped parents for when you were providing the service free previously?? Just seems strangely odd and greedy.

reviews.title: Don’t recommend
reviews.text: Started with this app last year as it was free to use and money is tight especially with me having to pay for family court and court related costs. Now  have been strong-armed by the app into paying for it by the app developers as I am unable to read messages regarding my child unless I pay for it! I understand that they may require more people to pay to keep the app going however, anyone still going through the process who has been using the free service before it incurred charges and for 1 year or more, should have still got it free. Added stress to an already stressful situation.

reviews.title: App Was great.
reviews.text: Have had the app for a couple years. And I never wrote in the messenger. It was for my husband and his child’s mother. I now cannot even view without being charged. I feel there should be away to still see the correspondence and only if I need to write or call be charged so the features and capabilities are weird. On top of that you cannot speak with anyone for help. My husband reached out months ago to get advice on how to pay for himself and me have read only access. Pretty strange it isn’t allowed. Very frustrating no one responds. Prior to this charge it was great now…not so much. Not worth it.

reviews.title: Demands money closes u down if u don’t pay .
reviews.text: Was made to believe it was free to use and keeps safe communications that are documented . Then suddenly demanded I have to pay to even have the app or it will be closed . This is dangerous for those told to use by courts for safety reasons and being told it’s free aswell from them . Money grabbers that will sting so many parents . Avoid .

reviews.title: Horrible
reviews.text: Used this app since it was free, the “options” for keeping everything in one place are horrible. Calendar doesn’t work all the time, glitches when putting in multiple days of parenting time (the co-parent is never consistent so it is done manually for the days they actually have the child) they’re now charging for this app which is a joke since it’s mediocre. I paid for two years, got the receipt and the next day got an email that I needed to get the subscription!! Paid again, they charged me twice. The only way to contact someone is email and it’s like no one checks it. This is scammy and I’m angry that I even have to deal with a refund

reviews.title: Used to be great
reviews.text: Used to be great until you decided to stick a large price tag on a subscription and both parties have to pay or in my case 3 people have to pay which is an absolute joke, if it was only one person paying for the app it wouldn’t be so bad but social workers and courts will not pay to use the app to be the third party.

reviews.title: Edit: Photo/video and update
reviews.text:
After over a year you still can’t add photo/video. It only Brings the selection screen up. Once you select a photo or video there’s no further prompts and the screen doesn’t change.   
The app overall is pretty broken, and painful to use. For being free it was at least usable for a difficult co parenting situation. However as of January 2026 they have transitioned to a paid subscription model. Which is not worth ANY amount of money, and has left us in an awkward predicament to find a new communication method. I highly suggest looking into other options, and if you’re able to pay for a communication app, or are simply out of free options. Just use our family wizard

reviews.title: Bait and Switch
reviews.text:
I’ve used AppClose for years only because it was free and convenient for co-parenting — but after their latest system “upgrade,” they decided to start charging without improving the product at all. The platform has never been stable: constant crashes, delayed messages, and notifications that don’t work. Every update somehow makes it worse.

Instead of fixing the basic reliability issues, AppClose chose to monetize a broken tool. That says everything about their priorities. Parents depend on this app for essential communication — and they’ve turned it into a glitchy cash grab.

Save yourself the frustration. There are better, more stable, and more transparent options out there.

reviews.title: Great but sadly now will be subscription only.
reviews.text: This app has been great to use with a combative coparent but now is required to have a subscription to use. I will stop using it and have to use another method instead as 100 a year is steep.

reviews.title: Not Free
reviews.text:
App is switching to paid service causing much stress for co parents in hostile situations. 

Especially ahead of court hearing in the new year. 

It was difficult enough to get the other parent to use a free app they are not willing to pay and now I will have to return to the stress of harassment via whatsapp. 

Really disappointed that this is happening in the midst of a cost of living crises, even for me the stress of yet another subscription is frustrating.
